note: Companies the long-term investing paper account may buy. Descriptions are a starting point from general knowledge (2026-11-16); the weekly research run checks and updates them, adds or removes companies, and records the date and sources it used. The trading rules only use prices; this list decides WHICH companies are eligible.

companies.name: NVIDIA
companies.what: Designs the graphics processors (GPUs) and networking used to train and run most AI models.
companies.risks: Very high expectations already in the price; customers building their own chips; export limits to China.

companies.name: Microsoft
companies.what: Windows, Office, the Azure cloud and a large stake in OpenAI's technology.
companies.potential: AI features sold to businesses through Azure and Office.
companies.risks: Huge AI data-centre costs; competition in cloud.

companies.name: Alphabet (Google)
companies.what: Google search and ads, YouTube, Google Cloud, its own AI models (Gemini) and AI chips (TPUs); also quantum computing research.
companies.potential: AI in search and cloud; quantum and self-driving (Waymo) as long-term options.
companies.risks: AI chatbots changing search habits; regulation.

companies.name: Amazon
companies.what: Online shop and AWS, the largest cloud provider; builds its own AI chips.

companies.name: Meta Platforms
companies.what: Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp; earns from ads; large AI research and open AI models.
companies.potential: Better ad targeting with AI; AI assistants.
companies.risks: Big spending on AI and virtual reality; regulation.

companies.name: Apple
companies.what: iPhone, Mac and services like the App Store.

companies.name: Broadcom
companies.what: Networking chips and custom AI chips for large cloud companies, plus infrastructure software.
companies.potential: Custom AI chips for Google, Meta and others.
companies.risks: Depends on a few big customers.

companies.name: AMD
companies.what: Processors for PCs and servers and AI accelerators competing with NVIDIA.
companies.potential: Winning a share of AI accelerator spending.

companies.name: TSMC
companies.what: Taiwanese company that manufactures most of the world's advanced chips, including NVIDIA's and Apple's.
companies.potential: Every AI chip maker needs it.

companies.name: ASML
companies.what: Dutch maker of the lithography machines needed to make advanced chips; near-monopoly in the most advanced machines.

companies.name: Palantir
companies.what: Data and AI software for governments and companies.
companies.potential: Companies adopting AI on their own data.
companies.risks: Very high valuation; big price swings.

companies.name: CrowdStrike
companies.potential: Security needs grow with cloud and AI.

companies.name: IonQ
companies.what: Builds quantum computers using trapped ions, sold through the cloud.
companies.potential: Could be large if quantum computers become useful.
companies.risks: Small revenue, losses; technology may take many years; extreme price swings.

companies.name: Rigetti Computing
companies.what: Builds superconducting quantum chips and computers.
companies.risks: Losses, needs funding; extreme price swings.

companies.name: D-Wave Quantum
companies.what: Quantum annealing computers for optimisation problems, sold as a cloud service.

companies.name: Invesco QQQ (Nasdaq-100 fund)
companies.what: A fund that holds the 100 largest non-financial Nasdaq companies.
companies.potential: Broad big-tech exposure in one purchase.
companies.risks: Falls with the whole tech market.

companies.name: VanEck Semiconductor fund
companies.what: A fund holding the largest chip companies.
